sections.heading: Coming to you because worship is life to me
sections.text: Glorious God, worshiping you is not a religious task I have to get through. It is what my life is for. To adore you is the deepest honor of my soul, and coming near to you is a joy I do not want to take lightly. Help me come to you now as you deserve—not distracted, not half-awake, but honestly and gladly before you.
theological_themes: Human beings are made to worship God, and true worship is both reverent and joyful.
Approaching God is a privilege, not a performance.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus teaches that the Father seeks true worshipers who worship in spirit and truth. This grounds the prayer’s desire for worship that is sincere, God-centered, and more than outward form.
David’s longing to dwell with the Lord and gaze on his beauty reflects the prayer’s sense that drawing near to God is the soul’s highest delight.

sections.heading: Asking the Spirit to help me worship
sections.text: Father, I cannot make my own heart alive to you. Give me help by your Holy Spirit. Quiet the noise of the world in me. Pull my attention back from what clamors for it. Bring me into the fullness of life that is found with you. Refresh me, steady me, comfort me, and bless me in your presence.
theological_themes: True worship depends on the Spirit’s enabling, not merely human effort.
God’s presence refreshes and strengthens his people amid worldly distractions.

scripture_references.connection: Paul says believers have access to the Father through Christ in one Spirit. This supports the prayer’s dependence on the Spirit for real approach to God.
The Spirit helps believers in their weakness and intercedes according to God’s will. This fits the request for divine help when the heart cannot worship rightly on its own.

sections.heading: Drawing near through Jesus, not hiding in fear
sections.text: Let me know your goodness so that your greatness does not drive me away in terror. Give me a clearer sight of Jesus—the Son of Man and Son of God. Because of him, I do not have to stay at a distance. He is my Mediator, my Brother, the one who makes you known, the promised Branch, the one who stands between me and judgment, the Lamb who was slain for me. In him I come near with the love of a child and the confidence you have given me. I praise him, and in him you lift me up.
theological_themes: God is majestic and holy, yet his goodness is revealed supremely in Christ.
Jesus is the Mediator who brings sinners near to God with childlike confidence.
Christ’s person and work remove terror and create holy boldness.

scripture_references.connection: Because Jesus is the great high priest, believers are invited to approach God’s throne with confidence for mercy and grace. This directly supports the movement from fear to holy boldness through Christ.
Paul identifies Jesus as the one Mediator between God and humanity, who gave himself as a ransom. This grounds the prayer’s reliance on Christ rather than self-protection or merit.
The Spirit gives believers the cry of adopted children rather than slavery to fear. This supports the prayer’s language of drawing near with filial love.

sections.heading: Giving back what was always yours
sections.text: I have no crown of my own to place before you. Anything worth offering is already a gift from you. So I give back what you have put in my hands—my life, my time, my loves, my work, my plans. Teach me to be content with this: that everything is most truly mine when it belongs to you, and that I gain it more deeply when I surrender it to you.
theological_themes: All that believers have comes from God and is returned to him in worship.
Surrender to God is not loss but the proper and joyful use of his gifts.

scripture_references.connection: David acknowledges that what God’s people offer to him already comes from his hand. This closely supports the prayer’s confession that there is nothing to give except what God first gave.
Paul calls believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, describing this as spiritual worship. This connects surrender of the whole self with worship.

sections.heading: Living wholly for my Savior
sections.text: Let me live fully for my Savior. Free me from the things that pull my heart apart—from restless anxiety, from unnecessary burdens, from anything that keeps me from walking the narrow road with you. Make my life simpler, steadier, and more devoted to Christ.
theological_themes: Following Christ requires undivided devotion and resistance to distractions.
Anxiety and worldly entanglements can hinder obedience and worship.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus describes the way that leads to life as narrow and difficult. This supports the prayer’s desire to keep pursuing that road without being turned aside.
Believers are told to lay aside sin and every weight while looking to Jesus. This fits the request to be freed from hindrances and distractions in following Christ.
Jesus warns against anxious preoccupation and calls his disciples to seek God’s kingdom first. This grounds the prayer’s request to be freed from consuming care.

sections.heading: Coming again to the cleansing blood of Jesus
sections.text: I have been forgiven through the blood of Jesus. Please make that mercy fresh to me again. Keep applying his finished work to my conscience as I confess my sins. Bring me every day to the fountain of his grace, and wash me again from the dirt I pick up along the way. Let that mercy make me a worshiper—not only now, but in all of life—in spirit and in truth.
theological_themes: Forgiveness rests on Christ’s blood, not on the believer’s worthiness.
Christ’s finished atonement continues to cleanse the believer’s conscience and restore fellowship with God.
Daily repentance and cleansing lead to ongoing worship.

scripture_references.connection: John teaches that the blood of Jesus cleanses believers from sin and that confession is met with God’s faithful forgiveness. This supports the prayer’s daily return to cleansing without implying Christ’s sacrifice must be repeated.
Believers draw near because of Jesus’ blood, with hearts cleansed from an evil conscience. This connects forgiveness, access to God, and worshipful nearness.

The prophet speaks of a fountain opened for cleansing from sin and uncleanness. In Christian interpretation this imagery naturally illuminates the prayer’s longing to return continually to God’s cleansing mercy.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original asks God to “continue to pardon me” and to be “washed anew” every day. I rendered this as the ongoing application of Christ’s finished work to confession, conscience, and fellowship, not as a repeated justification or repeated sacrifice.

The titles “Branch” and “Daysman” are older biblical/theological terms. “Branch” was retained as “the promised Branch”; “Daysman” was rendered as “the one who stands between me and judgment,” preserving the mediator idea without relying on an unfamiliar archaic word.
significant_interpretive_choices: “Give me knowledge of thy goodness that I might not be over-awed by thy greatness” was interpreted as a request to know God’s fatherly goodness in Christ so that reverence does not become servile terror.
“Everything is mine when it is thine” was rendered as surrender rather than ownership language, emphasizing that gifts are most rightly enjoyed when yielded back to God.
“Forget the world” was not rendered as contempt for creation or ordinary responsibilities, but as freedom from worldly noise and distractions during worship.
